content: For offline/deterministic eval of 'good advice' in an fdars advisor context, the established approach is a schema/structural-assertion layer: (1) deterministic: schema validity (Advice Pydantic model validates), evidence-citation check (_check_grounding already exists), diagnostic improvement metric (target_metric[after] > target_metric[before]) — pure Python, zero network, zero LLM, runs in CI every commit. (2) env-gated: multi-turn grounding quality (human or LLM judge, only runs with API key). No new library is needed — the grounding check pattern already exists in _validate.py; the auto-tuning eval is just: 'did the target diagnostic improve after the loop ran?' measured by comparing before/after build_diagnostics outputs. DeepEval and similar frameworks are heavyweight and overkill here.
